content.value_statement: Teams need consistent component styling without changing shared UI primitives. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create component CSS with Tailwind conventions and clear file boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to create a separate CSS file for each component.
Promotes Tailwind apply and component layer patterns for styling.
Directs agents to consult Tailwind 4.1 context docs when available.
Sets a target location for new component files.
Protects shared UI components from direct edits.
Recommends custom utilities and variants when the project needs them.
limitations: It provides instructions only, not reusable component templates.
It assumes the referenced Tailwind context docs exist in the target project.
The component path may be project-specific and should be verified before use.
It does not include accessibility, test, or state management guidance.

use_cases.title: Create Feature Components
use_cases.description: Build a new feature component with a separate CSS file and Tailwind component layer styling.

use_cases.title: Protect Shared UI Files
use_cases.description: Add project-specific components while keeping shared UI primitives unchanged.

use_cases.title: Apply Tailwind v4 Guidance
use_cases.description: Use project Tailwind context before styling a new interface element.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-components skill to create a new Tailwind component for [feature]. Follow the project component directory rules.

prompt_templates.title: Style an Existing Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-components skill to add a separate CSS file for [component]. Use Tailwind component layer conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Use Tailwind Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-components skill to review the Tailwind v4 context docs before styling [component]. Explain any assumptions before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Styling Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the designing-components skill to redesign [component] while preserving shared UI files. Add utilities or variants only when they fit existing conventions.

output_examples.input: Design a profile card component for a dashboard.
output_examples.output: The agent creates a new component, adds a nearby CSS file, and styles the card through Tailwind component layer guidance.

output_examples.input: Update a settings panel without changing shared UI primitives.
output_examples.output: The agent keeps protected UI files unchanged and adds feature-level styling in the component area.

output_examples.input: Add a custom visual state for a component.
output_examples.output: The agent checks project Tailwind context and uses custom utility or variant guidance only when it matches local conventions.

best_practices: Confirm the project uses Tailwind 4.1 before following Tailwind-specific context.
Keep component styles near the component and avoid changing shared UI primitives.
Review generated components for responsive behavior and accessibility states.
anti_patterns: Applying the skill to non-Tailwind projects without adapting the styling guidance.
Editing protected shared UI files when a feature-level component is enough.
Adding custom utilities or variants without checking existing project conventions.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents design frontend components with Tailwind-oriented CSS organization and clear file boundaries.

faq.question: Does it generate components by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions that Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can follow during implementation.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is built around Tailwind directives, component layers, utilities, and variants.

faq.question: Are the referenced Tailwind docs included?
faq.answer: The scanned skill package only includes SKILL.md, so target projects should provide those context files.

faq.question: Can it modify shared UI components?
faq.answer: The skill instructs agents not to touch the shared UI directory named in SKILL.md.
